headline: 9-wicket win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test in Darwin
summary: The Tigers turn a 23-year wait into a historic victory, dominating the hosts on their own soil for the first time in over two decades.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their biggest win in Test history. This victory ends a 23-year wait to return to Australian soil for Test cricket, dating back to their first tour in 2003.

The dominance began on the first morning when Hasan Mahmud ripped through the Australian batting line-up, taking 6-55 to dismiss the hosts for 198. Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain added two wickets each to complete the first-innings collapse.
In response, Bangladesh piled up 426 runs, creating a massive 228-run lead. Tanzid Hasan Tamim scored the first-ever Test century by a Bangladesh batter in Australia, a key milestone in the victory.

Despite a century from Cameron Green in the second innings, Mehidy Hasan Miraz took five wickets to ensure Australia could not mount a dangerous comeback. Bangladesh then calmly chased the target to win by nine wickets.

Australian captain Pat Cummins and batter Steve Smith admitted they were 'outplayed' by the disciplined performance of the the Tigers. Smith praised Bangladesh's discipline with both bat and ball throughout the four days.

This win is seen as a significant shift from previous overseas victories, as Bangladesh maintained control of the match from start to finish without relying on a single moment of magic or rain intervention.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! Bangladesh just dominated Australia on their own soil in a historic 9-wicket Test win.

Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their biggest win in Test history. This victory ends a 23-year wait to return to Australian soil for Test cricket, dating back to their first tour in 2003.

The dominance began on the first morning when Hasan Mahmud ripped through the Australian batting line-up, taking 6-55 to dismiss the hosts for 198. Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain added two wickets each to complete the first-innings collapse.

In response, Bangladesh piled up 426 runs, creating a massive 228-run lead. Tanzid Hasan Tamim scored the first-ever Test century by a Bangladesh batter in Australia, a key milestone in the victory.

Despite a century from Cameron Green in the second innings, Mehidy Hasan Miraz took five wickets to ensure Australia could not mount a dangerous comeback. Bangladesh then calmly chased the target to win by nine wickets.

Australian captain Pat Cummins and batter Steve Smith admitted they were 'outplayed' by the disciplined performance of the the Tigers. Smith praised Bangladesh's discipline with both bat and ball throughout the four days.

This win is seen as a significant shift from previous overseas victories, as Bangladesh maintained control of the match from start to finish without relying on a single moment of magic or rain intervention.

headline: Govt employees to get new pay scale within this year
summary: The Prime Minister's Principal Secretary says the structure is ready and the official announcement will be made anytime.
details: Prime Minister's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar confirmed that the new pay scale for government officials and employees will be implemented within this year.
Speaking at a press briefing at the Secretariat on Sunday, he stated that the entire structure for the new pay scale is ready and the government will make the official announcement at any time.

The Principal Secretary noted that while the pay scale increase will create economic pressure on the government's budget, the government plans to manage this through the creation of new employment opportunities.
He also acknowledged that the pay scale increase may lead to temporary inflation in the market, which he described as a reality that must be accepted.
The government will attempt to mitigate the effect of this inflation through various alternative policies and initiatives.

Additionally, the Principal Secretary addressed the energy crisis, describing it electricity and fuel shortages as a major challenge. He attributed the crisis to the long-term mismanagement and whims of the previous government.
He assured that sustainable solutions to the country's fuel problem will be achieved in the shortest possible time through effective measures taken by the current government.
caption:

The government will attempt to mitigate the effect of this inflation through various alternative policies and initiatives.
